hook.text: The old stack was one vendor for everything. The modern stack lets you swap any piece without rebuilding.

buildup.text: Composable architecture means each layer — ingestion, storage, transform, serve — is an independent tool.

discovery.text: Standardized interfaces and open formats like Parquet let tools interoperate without tight coupling.

twist.text: Composability creates integration overhead. Getting 5 tools to work together requires glue code and monitoring.

climax.text: The trade-off is clear: composable stacks are flexible but complex. Monoliths are simple but rigid.

punchline.text: Swap any piece. But maintain every connection.

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off of a composable data stack?
